findings.evidence: Also, you submit the request in the portal. Countersign the employee request within two business days. You track its status there until the payment clears.
findings.fix: Give the countersigning sentence its own explicit subject, such as the manager countersigns the employee's request within two business days, so the reader is never asked to perform an action that is not theirs.
findings.violation: The paragraph addresses the employee directly as you in the first and third sentences, then switches with no signal to a bare imperative, countersign the employee request, that only the approving manager can act on; a reader cannot tell which instructions are theirs to act on.

findings.evidence: Employees keep proof of purchase for every stipend item. ... Finance reconciles the reimbursable item against the request log each month. Payroll releases the covered purchase amount after that monthly review.
findings.fix: Pick one term for the reimbursed purchase and one term for the log, and use each consistently throughout, replacing reimbursable item and covered purchase with stipend item and reconciling reimbursement log against request log into a single name.
findings.violation: Stipend item, reimbursable item, and covered purchase name what appears to be the same reimbursed purchase, and reimbursement log versus request log name what may be the same record or two different ones, with no defined-terms section or stated equivalence anywhere in the document; a reader cannot tell whether these are the same thing or different things.

findings.evidence: Then, the employee reviews the confirmation summary before submitting the final request. The summary shows the equipment cost and the requested delivery date.
findings.fix: Reorder the section so the review-before-submitting step appears before the signing, budget-confirmation, and processing steps, matching the order the employee actually performs them in.
findings.violation: This sentence places reviewing the summary before submitting the final request after the prior paragraph has already described the request moving through signing, budget confirmation, final processing, and a confirmation email, so the section's own step order contradicts the sequence a reader would actually have to perform the steps in, and a reader following the section in order would submit before reviewing.

findings.evidence: The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout.
findings.fix: Rewrite the opening sentence to state the topic the rest of the paragraph covers.
findings.violation: The paragraph's opening sentence shares almost no vocabulary with the rest of the paragraph, so it does not preview the paragraph's actual topic.

findings.evidence: The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout. A separate audit last spring reviewed unrelated travel expenses. Federal guidance on remote work continues to evolve each year. The office coffee budget was reset at the start of the quarter.
findings.fix: Remove the three unrelated sentences from this section, or if they belong in the document at all, give each its own section with its own heading rather than folding them into Program Coordination.
findings.violation: After its first sentence states the section's apparent topic, the section's remaining three sentences pursue three unrelated themes (a past travel-expense audit, federal remote-work guidance, and the office coffee budget) with nothing connecting any of them to stipend coordination or to each other, so a reader finishing the section could not state what it was actually about.

findings.evidence: The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout. A separate audit last spring reviewed unrelated travel expenses. Federal guidance on remote work continues to evolve each year. The office coffee budget was reset at the start of the quarter.
findings.fix: Rewrite the paragraph so each sentence's subject connects back to the one before it, or split the unrelated sentences into their own passages with their own topic sentences.
findings.violation: Each of the four sentences introduces a wholly new subject (the benefits team, a separate audit, federal guidance, the office coffee budget) that the prior sentence gave no basis for, with no sentence picking up the topic the one before it just established, so the reader has to re-orient at every sentence boundary.

findings.evidence: Also, the stipend request, once the manager signs it, after finance confirms the budget line, moves to final processing.
findings.fix: Move the interrupting clause elsewhere, or split it into its own sentence.
findings.violation: 3 comma-set-off clause(s) totalling 14 words intervene between the sentence's apparent subject and its verb.

findings.evidence: An incomplete request pauses the timeline until the missing item arrives. The...
findings.fix: Open the paragraph with a transition word that states its relationship to the prior paragraph.
findings.violation: The paragraph opens with none of the fixed transition words, so the reader is not told how it relates to the paragraph before it.

findings.evidence: Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and the uploaded receipt.
findings.fix: Name the employee as the subject, for example the employee completes the request by confirming eligibility and uploading a receipt.
findings.violation: The sentence's subject is the abstraction completing the request rather than the employee who actually confirms eligibility and uploads the receipt, standing in for an identifiable actor the rest of the document names directly elsewhere.

findings.evidence: Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and the uploaded receipt.
findings.fix: Restate every item in the series with the same grammatical form.
findings.violation: The series' 2 items mix grammatical forms (gerund, other) at their head words instead of sharing one form.

findings.evidence: The employee receives a confirmation email once processing finishes.
findings.fix: Reorder the sentence to end on the new information, for example once processing finishes, the employee receives a confirmation email.
findings.violation: The sentence's newest element, a confirmation email, is introduced mid-sentence and then followed by once processing finishes, information the prior sentence already gave the reader, so the sentence ends on already-known material instead of on the new element.
